🇳🇵 Kathmandu Police have taken 36 Chinese nationals - 31 men and five women - into custody from the White Park Resort in Shikharpur. During the search of two rooms, authorities seized around 50 mobile phones, several laptops and more than 100 other electronic devices. Of those, 36 mobile phones have been formally logged as evidence.

🔊 FBI Director says US tech outages are inevitable — blames previous administrations FBI Director Kash Patel is addressing the catastrophic string of nationwide system failures by claiming that "technical disruptions" are simply unavoidable, while pointing the finger at the previous administration for leaving behind "legacy" systems. 💬 "There will be some technical disruptions like what we've seen... Legacy meaning other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn't. We are. We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time." It has taken the current administration nearly two years to even begin updating the nation's critical infrastructure. The timing is brutally ironic: they finally start patching the network, and the entire country's banking and aviation systems immediately crash. The FAA grounded thousands of flights because of a router bought in 2001. Banks froze because of ancient backend systems. Yet, instead of taking responsibility for a crumbling domestic grid, Patel is deflecting to the private sector and vowing to "hunt down nefarious actors" all over the world. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
